📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Corsair's AIR 5400 RS-R midtower PC case is down to its lowest price ever, with a 31% discount bringing the price down to $169.99. The case normally retails for nearly $250, and outside of a short sale last month, we haven't seen it drop below $200. In addition, with a wrap-around glass side panel and triple-chamber design, the case comes with three Corsair RS-R 120mm PWM ARGB fans, which normally run $60 on their own.

Typical of these multi-chamber case designs, the AIR 5400 RS-R supports most hardware you can throw at it. You can use anything from a mini ITX motherboard to an E-ATX board, and it has mounting points for up to two 360mm radiators, plus an additional 120mm mounting point. The 360mm worth of mounting space on the bottom of the case is occupied by the pre-installed fans and an airflow shroud.

Recent findings suggest that additionally, the case is compatible with rear-connector motherboards from Asus, MSI, and Gigabyte, so you can have a cable-free front chamber. The case doesn't have a vertical GPU mount, but there's ample room for even larger graphics cards, with a maximum length of 430 mm supported. Like most multi-chamber cases, this one is primarily designed around liquid cooling. However, you have a generous 180mm of CPU cooler clearance if you decide to go with an air cooler.

The Corsair AIR 5400 RS-R is a midtower PC case with three Corsair RS-R 120mm ARGB fans pre-installed. It supports up to E-ATX motherboards, as well as rear-connector boards from MSI, Asus, and Gigabyte.

In a recent development, the Corsair AIR 1500 RS-R is loaded with enough features to justify its $250 list price, let alone its current sale price of $170. In addition to wide cooling and GPU compatibility, along with rear-connector motherboard support, the case comes with a built-in anti-sag arm to support your GPU, the height of which you can adjust depending on your GPU. Be warned, however, that the final fan on especially long GPUs may hit the support. Thankfully, you can remove it.

Sources indicate that corsair includes its RapidRoute 2.0 mounting system, giving you a pegboard-style motherboard tray that provides mounting points virtually anywhere for cable management. Cable managing multi-chamber cases is much easier than a traditional tower, as well, with ample room behind the motherboard tray to hide your cable mess.

In a recent development, around the front, the curved-glass side panel highlights off the internals of your rig from the side and front. To get inside, the curved panel splits apart like French doors, so you can service your machine without juggling a few different pieces of tempered glass. The rear side panel is on a hinge for easy access, as well.

Recent findings suggest that the one major downside with this chassis is that it doesn't come with any front panel USB-A ports. Instead, you get three USB-C ports, split between two USB 3.2 Gen 1 ports and a single Gen 2 port, alongside a 3.5mm headphone/microphone combo jack. Given that most motherboards have one or maybe two USB-C ports, extra front panel connectors are always nice to have. However, even a single USB-A would go a long way.

Google’s Fitbit Air is one of my favorite products of 2026 and my preferred workout companion, but not being able to see a workout while you’re in the middle of it has been a huge complaint of mine, and the latest Google Health enhancement is fixing that.

Quite literally at the start of this week, I was on a walk through my neighborhood and though to myself, “it’s still pretty annoying that I can’t see my workout progress in the Google Health app.” It’s been a complaint of mine for a while, as various treadmill sessions and more have left me wondering what my heart rate is looking like, how many steps I’ve taken, etc, and it’s only a problem when using the Fitbit Air, seeing as the Pixel Watch (or Fitbit Edge) I’d wear otherwise will show that data front and center.

Google Health 5.13 is fixing that.

In the changelog for Google Health 5.13, Google details a upcoming “exercise in-progress” card on the main “Today” screen. This will show what exercise is being tracked and also let you end the workout early.

According to recent reports, if you use your Pixel Watch, Fitbit Air, or Fitbit Edge to automatically track your exercises, you’ll now see an exercise-in-progress card on your mobile app’s Today screen. This card lets you know that your device is tracking your exercise and gives you the opportunity to end the tracking and get your summary whenever you want.

We don’t know exactly what this card looks like just yet, but it sounds like it fits the need perfectly.

Google Health 5.13 is now rolling out on Android and iOS.

Sources indicate that intel's popular Core i7-14700K remains one of the best CPUs for gaming, and it's currently on sale for its lowest price ever at $249.99. The Raptor Lake Refresh CPU ranks well in our CPU benchmark hierarchy, despite being a last-gen chip, and it slots into LGA 1700 motherboards, which are available in both DDR5 and DDR4 varieties. Critically, the Core i7-14700K offers 97% of the gaming performance of the more expensive Core i9-14900K, which is currently selling for $150 more.

Industry observers note that when Black Friday sales first spun up, we saw the Core i7-14700K drop to $249.99 at Amazon, and that deal sold out in less than 24 hours. Newegg has the chip available for $299.99, but B&H is at the moment matching the Amazon price. The sale likely won't last long (especially after publishing this article), so you'll want to act fast to get the chip at this price. B&H itself warns that there's "limited supply at this price.".

The CPU doesn't include a boxed cooler, so you'll need to bring your own. It's unlocked for overclocking, however, given that you slot it into a Z-series motherboard.

As part of the sale, Intel has thrown in its holiday gaming bundle, which allows you to choose two free games out of the following titles: Total War Warhammer 40K, Star Wars Galactic Racer, Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, Lego Batman Legacy of the Dark Knight, Everwind, Battlefield 6, or Assassin's Creed Shadows.

Get 20 total cores, eight performance, and 12 efficiency, with 28 threads and Intel UHD Graphics 770 included.

The Core i7-14700K has become a particularly popular CPU in the past several months, mainly due to DDR5 shortages. Earlier in the year, Intel told us that Raptor Lake remained a critical part of Intel's portfolio, and that it would be that way for "years to come." Now, we're finally seeing the result of promised pricing and inventory adjustments, with the Core i7-14700K dropping to its lowest price ever.

As you can see from the charts above, the Core i7-14700K remains a potent CPU in both gaming and productivity applications, falling short in the former mainly to AMD's X3D chips. Even in the face of latest Arrow Lake Refresh offerings, 14th-gen CPUs offer competitive performance, and sometimes at a lower price. You get additional upside, too, with support for DDR4 and DDR5 motherboards.

Sources indicate that we explored the performance delta between DDR4 and DDR5 on Intel's 14th-gen CPUs, and with the Core i7-14700K, we saw an average drop of 13% in games at 1080p following our normal CPU test suite. That's a significant performance loss, but the Core i7-14700K still manages to match the gaming performance of the Ryzen 7 5800X3D, which is otherwise the fastest DDR4 gaming CPU on the market.

The Core i7-14700K slots into existing LGA 1700 motherboards, though you'll need a Z-series chipset if you want to manually overclock the chip. Although Intel has moved on from the LGA 1700 socket, reports suggest the company is working on new 'Raptor Lake Next' chips that will use the same socket.

What Is the Best UI design Tool? 8 Tools Compared by the Job They Do (2026)

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the ideal UI testing tool is the one that discovers what your users discover first: broken layouts, usability issues that no longer work, and new accessibility issues in all the browsers your users use before a change goes into the repository.
  • Sources indicate that even with the right stack, it still relies on what your team needs to catch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

According to recent reports, the ideal UI testing tool is the one that discovers what your users discover first: broken layouts, usability issues that no longer work, and new accessibility issues in all the browsers your users use before a change goes into the repository. In 2026, most frontend teams don't rely on a single tool to do all of that. The best setups involve two layers: a test runner layer that launches the browser and monitors behavior, and a UI testing and review platform that visually checks the outcome and routes changes to the right stakeholders for sign-off.

Sources indicate that even with the right stack, it still relies on what your team needs to catch. Different teams will focus on different points: a QA team trying to automate checkout flows, a design system team defending shared components, and a single developer working on a tight budget will all be somewhere different. This guide is categorized by the job these UI testing tools do, then connects them.

Most "best UI testing tool" lists rank test runners and visual testing platforms against each other as if they were interchangeable. They aren't. UI testing covers four distinct jobs:.

Functional testing: Does the UI respond correctly when a user clicks, types, or hovers?

Visual testing: Does the UI still look right across layout, color, typography, and spacing?

Accessibility testing: Can people using keyboards and screen readers use it, and did this change introduce upcoming violations?

Cross-browser and device coverage: Does it work in Safari on mobile, not just Chrome on a developer's laptop?

There are also other levels of UI tests. Unit tests test the logic but don't interact with the UI. End-to-end (E2E) tests represent the full user journey in a browser but are difficult to set up, hard to troubleshoot when the bug is a visual detail, and can't practically test every state. Between the extremes of unit tests and E2E tests, component tests simulate each component's behavior in a real browser using fixed inputs, offering speed closer to unit tests and user-level coverage closer to E2E. Many teams maintain a thin layer of E2E tests for critical journeys, and they have component tests for the dozens of states a component may be in.

These tools are organized by job so you can stack them rather than choose one winner.

These platforms sit on top of your test runner. They capture rendered UI, compare it to approved baselines, and give your team a place to review what changed.

Sources indicate that chromatic is a UI testing and review platform made by the Storybook team. It catches visual, interaction, and accessibility bugs in components and pages before they merge, and it gives developers, designers, and product managers one place to review UI changes and sign off. Chromatic's team is the core maintainer of Storybook, which has about 90,000 GitHub stars and 17 million weekly npm downloads, and a Vitest core maintainer on the team built Chromatic's Vitest integration. Chromatic is used by 45 Fortune 100 companies, including GitHub, Shopify, Microsoft, Adobe, the BBC, and monday.com.

Sources indicate that pricing: Free plan with 5,000 snapshots per month (Chrome only), unlimited projects and people. Starter is $179/month for 35,000 snapshots and adds Safari, Firefox, and Edge. Pro is $399/month for 85,000 snapshots. Enterprise is custom, with SSO, SCIM, SLA support, and data retention. TurboSnap snapshots count as 0.2 of a regular snapshot.

Trade-offs: Chromatic is strongest when your UI is built from components. Teams with no component tests can start from Playwright or Cypress E2E tests, but they'll get the most value once components are covered too. Snapshot usage also grows with each browser and viewport you add, so initiative coverage before you scale it.

Best for: Design system teams, product teams that want designers and PMs to approve UI changes, React Native teams, and Vitest-first teams that want visual testing without baselines stored in the repo.

Percy is BrowserStack's visual testing platform. It captures screenshots from your existing tests, renders them across browsers and responsive widths, and highlights pixel differences for review.

In a recent development, strengths: Framework-agnostic SDKs for Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, and Storybook. App Percy covers native mobile apps. The free strategy includes 5,000 screenshots per month with unlimited users and projects.

Recent findings suggest that trade-offs: Percy is page-oriented, and each page rendered in each browser at each width counts as a separate screenshot, so usage climbs quickly with cross-browser coverage. Percy compares feature branches against a base branch, which teams with complex branching should test early. Reviewers see rendered screenshots rather than an inspectable copy of the code under test, so debugging a diff usually means reproducing it locally.

Pricing: Free tier, then paid intends with fixed screenshot allowances and overage.

Best for: Teams already paying for BrowserStack that want visual checks on page-level E2E tests.

Applitools Eyes uses Visual AI to compare screenshots the way a person would, with match levels that can ignore content changes and focus on layout. Its Ultrafast Grid re-renders captured page states across many browser, viewport, and device combinations.

Strengths: Mature AI matching, broad browser and device coverage, Figma and Storybook testing, accessibility testing, and an MCP server. Higher tiers add AI-driven functional testing and plain-English test authoring.

According to recent reports, trade-offs: Applitools is priced and packaged for enterprises. There's a free trial but no free strategy, and the Starter plan is $667/month billed annually for 100,000 component checkpoints or 1,000 page checkpoints. Professional and Enterprise are custom-priced.

Best for: Large QA organizations with big cross-browser matrices and budget for a dedicated visual AI platform.

BackstopJS is a free, open-source visual regression testing tool released under the MIT license. You list the URLs, viewports, and CSS selectors to capture in a config file, and BackstopJS renders them in a headless browser through Playwright or Puppeteer, then compares the results against approved reference screenshots. The core workflow runs on three commands: backstop init, backstop test, and backstop approve.

Strengths: Completely free, with no screenshot limits. A built-in browser report shows reference and test images side by side with a visual diff inspector, and changes can be approved from there. Optional Docker rendering keeps screenshots consistent between laptops and CI; Playwright adds Firefox and WebKit, and click, hover, and keypress selectors capture interactive states. JUnit reports plug into existing CI pipelines.

Trade-offs: BackstopJS is self-hosted, so there's no cloud dashboard, shared team review, or pull request status checks out of the box. Reference screenshots are usually committed to your repository, and every page or component state you want to test needs its own URL and scenario in the config. Someone on the team also has to own the setup, CI integration, and maintenance.

Best for: Developers and small teams with no budget who are comfortable running and maintaining their own visual regression setup.

Test runners click, type, and assert. They're free and open source, and every platform above builds on them. On their own, they offer limited visual testing: built-in screenshot assertions store baselines in your repository, rendering can drift between laptops and CI, and designers have no review interface.

In a recent development, playwright is Microsoft's open-source browser automation framework. It runs tests across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, with auto-waiting, trace viewer debugging and code generation, and supports JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, and .NET.

Industry observers note that visual testing: Playwright's toHaveScreenshot assertion compares screenshots against baselines stored in Git. It works, but baselines must be regenerated per operating system, and accepting a change means rerunning with an update flag.

Industry observers note that best for: Teams automating critical user journeys such as sign-up, checkout and login. Pair it with a platform like Chromatic for visual review across real browsers.

Cypress is an open-source testing tool that runs inside the browser, with time-travel debugging that shows the app at each step of a test. It supports both E2E and component testing.

According to recent reports, visual testing: Cypress has no built-in visual comparison and relies on plugins or a platform such as Chromatic, Percy or Applitools. Cypress Cloud, its paid service, adds recording, parallelization, flake detection and add-ons for accessibility and UI coverage.

Best for: Frontend developers who want fast feedback and an interactive test runner while they build.

Industry observers note that storybook is the open source workshop for building UI components in isolation. Each story captures one component state, and those stories double as test cases.

Testing features: Interaction tests with play functions and Testing Library, accessibility checks with the a11y addon, and a Vitest integration that runs stories as component tests.

Recent findings suggest that visual testing: Storybook doesn't diff screenshots on its own. Chromatic, built by the same team, is its visual testing and review layer.

Best for: Design system and component library teams, and any team practicing component-driven development.

Vitest Browser Mode runs component tests in a real browser instead of a simulated DOM, using Playwright or WebdriverIO under the hood.

Industry observers note that visual testing: Vitest's toMatchScreenshot assertion stores screenshots in the repository. For large projects, this can bloat the repo and baselines drift between machines. Chromatic can take Vitest Browser Mode tests with no code changes and run them in a stable cloud environment instead.

Best for: Teams already writing Vitest tests who want them to check how the UI looks without adopting a new framework.

Start from the problem your team is trying to fix:.

"Shared component changes keep breaking other teams' screens." Test at the component level with Storybook or Vitest Browser Mode and Chromatic, so the change shows up on the pull request that caused it.

"Our Playwright tests pass, but the layout still breaks in Safari." Functional assertions don't check appearance. Add a visual testing platform that renders in Safari, such as Chromatic, Percy or Applitools.

"We turned off screenshot tests because of false alarms." Look for deterministic component states and flake controls such as Chromatic's SteadySnap, or AI matching such as Applitools.

"Designers find UI bugs after release." Choose a platform with a review and approval workflow, and make sign-off a required pull request check.

"AI coding agents keep inventing components." Give agents access to your real component library, for example through Chromatic's hosted MCP, and run every agent-built change through the same UI tests as human code.

"We have no budget." Use Playwright or Vitest screenshot assertions, self-host BackstopJS, or start on the free tiers of Chromatic or Percy.

A practical, well-covered setup for a React web app looks like this:.

Unit tests in Vitest for logic and utilities.

Storybook stories or Vitest Browser Mode tests for every meaningful component state, with interaction tests on key components.

Chromatic running visual, interaction and accessibility tests on those components in Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge on every pull request, with designers assigned as reviewers.

A thin layer of Playwright E2E tests for sign-up, checkout and other critical journeys, also captured in Chromatic so page-level visual changes go through the same review.

This keeps most UI coverage in fast, deterministic component tests, while E2E tests confirm the journeys that matter most still work end to end.

According to recent reports, playwright is the best free tool for E2E UI testing, and Storybook is the best free tool for testing component states. For visual testing, For visual testing, Chromatic and Percy both offer free tiers of around 5,000 snapshots or screenshots per month, and BackstopJS is free to self-host.

UI testing is the broad practice of checking that an interface works for users, including functional, visual and accessibility checks. Visual testing is one part of it: comparing rendered UI against approved baselines to catch unintended changes in layout, color, typography and spacing.

It has been revealed that no. Chromatic was built by the Storybook team, but it also runs visual tests from Vitest Browser Mode, Playwright and Cypress tests, and from React Native Storybook on iOS and Android simulators.

Industry observers note that playwright's toHaveScreenshot covers basic visual checks, but baselines live in your repo, rendering can differ between machines, and there's no review interface for designers. Teams with several reviewers or many browsers usually add a platform on top.

Recent findings suggest that most teams use both. Component tests cover individual UI states quickly and reliably, while a smaller set of E2E tests confirms that critical user journeys work across the whole app.

Sources indicate that it’s been nearly three years since Best Buy decided to ditch selling physical copies of movies, stripping its inventory from both its brick-and-mortar stores and its online catalog. But with the growing rise of 4K Blu-ray collections as a vinyl-esque collector’s item, the electronics giant has slowly begun dipping its toes back into the physical media game.

Industry observers note that as spotted by TheHDRoom on Twitter and on the 4K Blu-ray subreddit, Best Buy is now selling 14 different 4K Blu-rays on its website, marking another step in the brand’s slow return to selling physical media. These films include:.

According to recent reports, technically, Blu-ray returned to Best Buy’s online storefront in August of 2025, when it opened a third-party marketplace similar to Amazon or Walmart. These titles, however, are shipped and sold by Best Buy. Everything’s still online-only, unfortunately, save for The Odyssey, which launched in-store shelf displays alongside yesterday’s release date. It shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise that The Odyssey is getting some special treatment; in addition to its status as a box office juggernaut, Nolan’s previous movie, Oppenheimer, initially sold out of physical copies in its first week of release in 2023.

Outside of these 14 titles, additional Blu-rays continue to be sold through Best Buy’s third-party marketplace.

It really doesn’t matter what content you come across – the wider inner display gives you that large screen feeling.

According to recent reports, like a well-designed tool, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 has more purposes than the tasks best suited for the inner display. That shorter, wider profile makes the outer display smaller, but not as thin as something on other foldables, like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra.

In reality, the aspect ratio is similar enough across both the inner and outer screens that most content scales well on the shorter front panel. Social apps like X and Instagram look great because videos and images are able to fill the screen, rather than squeeze. Samsung’s One UI software also supports app optimization across both screens, although the experience may vary by app.

Recent findings suggest that saying the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s outer display is “minimal” isn’t a dig, either. Apps can be refreshing to use when you don’t need to open them on a large scale. Take Messages, for instance. It’s not a complex app, and there isn’t a ton to see – just the last couple of messages exchanged. The same goes for plenty of apps available on the Google Play Store.

It has been revealed that and guess what? If you don’t like using the app on a smaller display, just unfold the phone. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is such a versatile phone, whether it’s a gift during the holidays or one for yourself.

There are instances where you need the large real estate. One UI 9 gives the Galaxy Z Fold 8 the option to open and run multiple apps on your screen. There are several ways you can do it, too.

It has been revealed that the main approach is to split two apps on the wide inner display. But if you want to see more from one app, you can simply drag the split over in one direction. One UI 9 leaves room to add one more app to that split screen, giving you a three-way Split View. All it takes is dragging an app from the taskbar and choosing the spot.

If you truly need a fourth app open, you have the option to open another in a floating window. Having four apps open at once is definitely a niche instance, but the Galaxy Z Fold 8 handles it like it’s nothing. You can have YouTube up in one corner while you check Messages for gift ideas and shop through the Amazon app. It might be helpful to keep a list of what you got and for whom in a floating Sheets window.

Recent findings suggest that the point is not only that it’s technically possible, but it’s usable. So often devices let users open apps in split screen, but are in no way comfortable enough for the task. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is perfect for it, and the experience actually makes you more productive, not less.

Sources indicate that most phones don’t let you get the best angle without any sort of third-party accessory. The Galaxy Z Fold 8, though, acts like its own tripod in a way.

Think of how many times you wanted to get a good angle on a plane or somewhere where there’s this flat surface just asking for a tiny tripod or kickstand. Well, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is its own kickstand and can be positioned at just the right angle.

Build Live Video Chat With WebRTC: From First Call to Production Debugging

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1210 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sitepoint

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • Industry observers note that weekly.
  • In a recent development, 7 Day Free Trial.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Industry observers note that weekly. Free. One click to leave.

In a recent development, 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Adding real-time video to a web app used to mean plugins, proprietary SDKs and a lot of money. Today every modern browser ships with WebRTC, a set of APIs that lets two browsers exchange audio, video and data directly. The catch is that WebRTC gives you building blocks, not a finished feature. This guide walks through those blocks in the order you actually need them, with the exact API calls you need, and then covers the production issues that tutorials usually skip.

A browser-to-browser call has four moving parts:.

Industry observers note that start with the local preview. Browsers only allow camera access on HTTPS or localhost, so serve your page accordingly.

1. Request a stream with navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia(), passing video constraints (an ideal width of 1280 and height of 720 is a sensible default) and audio constraints with echoCancellation and noiseSuppression enabled.

Sources indicate that 2. Assign the returned MediaStream to the srcObject property of your local video element.

In a recent development, 3. Keep a reference to the stream, because you will add its tracks to the peer connection later.

Industry observers note that set the muted and playsinline attributes on the local video element. Without muted users hear themselves, and without playsinline iOS Safari opens the video full screen.

According to recent reports, the peers need a way to find each other. A tiny Node.js server using the ws package is enough for development. Its whole job is to relay messages between the peers in a room:.

1. Create a WebSocket server (for example with the ws package) listening on its own port.

Sources indicate that 2. Keep a map of room names to the set of sockets in each room.

3. When a client sends a join message, store the room name on the socket and add it to that room's set.

4. For every other message type, forward the raw message to the other sockets in the same room, and never echo it back to the sender.

According to recent reports, 5. On disconnect, remove the socket from its room so stale peers do not receive messages.

In production you would add authentication, limit room size to two for one-to-one calls, and validate message types, but the shape stays the same.

Both sides create an RTCPeerConnection, add their local tracks and listen for the remote ones:.

Industry observers note that 1. Create a newly introduced RTCPeerConnection with an iceServers list that contains at least one STUN server.

Recent findings suggest that 2. Loop over the local stream's tracks and call addTrack() for each one.

3. In the ontrack handler, attach the first remote stream to your remote video element.

Recent findings suggest that 4. In the onicecandidate handler, send every fresh candidate to the other peer through your signalling channel as a candidate message.

One peer creates an offer, the other answers, and both apply each other's descriptions. Candidates arrive asynchronously in the background.

1. The caller runs createOffer(), applies it with setLocalDescription() and sends the description as an offer message.

2. The callee applies the offer with setRemoteDescription(), runs createAnswer(), applies it locally and sends it back as an answer.

3. The caller applies the answer with setRemoteDescription().

4. Both sides pass every incoming candidate message to addIceCandidate().

It has been revealed that if both peers might start a call at the same time, look up the "perfect negotiation" pattern on MDN. It assigns one side as polite and resolves offer collisions cleanly instead of leaving both peers stuck.

On a home network, STUN alone often works. On corporate Wi-Fi, mobile carriers and symmetric NATs it frequently does not, and the call silently fails to connect. A TURN server relays media when a direct path is impossible. The open-source coturn server is the usual choice.

In practice, your iceServers list should contain your own STUN URL plus a TURN URL with a username and credential, so the browser can fall back to the relay automatically when direct connectivity fails.

Generate short-lived TURN credentials on your backend rather than hard-coding them, and budget for bandwidth: relayed calls pass every frame through your server.

Owners deny camera access, unplug headsets and switch from Wi-Fi to 4G mid-call. Catch NotAllowedError and show a clear explanation, listen for devicechange events, and use RTCRtpSender.replaceTrack() to swap cameras without renegotiating the whole call.

It has been revealed that listen to pc.onconnectionstatechange. When the state becomes disconnected, wait a few seconds before giving up, because it often recovers. On failed, call pc.restartIce() to try fresh network paths.

Use RTCRtpSender.setParameters() to cap the bitrate on weak connections, and read pc.getStats() to monitor packet loss and round-trip time. Showing a small "poor connection" indicator does more for perceived quality than any codec tweak.

Mesh calls, where every participant connects to every other, work for two or three people. Beyond that, upload bandwidth explodes. Group calls need a Selective Forwarding Unit (SFU) such as mediasoup, LiveKit or Janus, which receives each stream once and forwards it to the others.

Tutorials end at a working demo, but the fastest way to understand what production WebRTC looks like is to watch a real call from the inside. Chrome ships an internal diagnostics page that demonstrates every peer connection the browser opens, and it works on any site that uses WebRTC.

1. Open chrome://webrtc-internals in one tab and keep it open.

2. In another tab, start a call on your own demo and find its RTCPeerConnection entry.

3. Expand that entry and look at the ICE candidate pairs: you will see whether the call went direct (host or srflx) or through a TURN relay (relay).

According to recent reports, 4. Open the stats graphs for the outbound video stream and watch the bitrate, frame rate and resolution adapt when you throttle the network in DevTools.

5. Check the negotiated codec and how quickly the connection recovers when you switch Wi-Fi off and back on.

Recent findings suggest that once you can read your own call, repeat the exercise on a production service. Any browser-based product works, whether a meeting tool or a live video chat that pairs two visitors, because webrtc-internals demonstrates the same data for every site. Expect differences from your demo: more candidate pairs, a relay candidate in the list and a bitrate that adapts faster. Seeing them makes the earlier sections concrete, from why TURN matters to how bandwidth estimation reacts to packet loss.

The one-to-one call above is the core of many products, from telehealth consultations and tutoring to customer support. The engineering challenges grow with the use case: random matching needs queueing and presence on the signalling server, public platforms need moderation and reporting, and global audiences need TURN servers in several regions.

Industry observers note that start with the minimal version, get it working across Chrome, Firefox and Safari on both desktop and mobile, and add TURN before real customers arrive. Once the call is reliable, every other feature becomes a much easier problem.

NFL forced Saquon Barkley to sell Polymarket stake, treating prediction markets as sportsbooks

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readwrite

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eagles running back Saquon Barkley sold his equity stake in Polymarket after NFL rules barred players from holding prediction-market investments.
  • Industry observers note that saquon Barkley no longer owns a piece of Polymarket.
  • Industry observers note that barkley bought into Polymarket before the league told players they could not hold such investments.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eagles running back Saquon Barkley sold his equity stake in Polymarket after NFL rules barred players from holding prediction-market investments. The case sets the league apart from the NBA and MLB, which have signed deals with the exchanges, as the NFL argues at the Supreme Court that sports event contracts are gambling.

Industry observers note that saquon Barkley no longer owns a piece of Polymarket. The Eagles running back sold his equity stake to comply with league rules, he told Front Office Sports in an interview published October 28. It is the first public case of the NFL applying its gambling rules to a player’s prediction-market investment.

Industry observers note that barkley bought into Polymarket before the league told players they could not hold such investments. The NFL goes over endorsement, investment and training rules with players before every season.

The league has now made clear that its sportsbook restrictions extend to prediction markets. It declined to comment on Barkley’s case specifically. The stance was not new to players. Kalshi and Polymarket were already off-limits to them as endorsers or brand ambassadors in January 2026. At that point, prediction markets were treated as gambling entities under the league’s gambling policy.

According to recent reports, the NFL’s approach puts it at odds with other major leagues. Polymarket became Major League Baseball’s Official Prediction Market Exchange on March 19, 2026. On October 26, 2026, the NBA named both companies its preferred prediction-market exchanges. The agreement gives them rights to league intellectual property and marketing.

It has been revealed that NBA players face far lighter limits. They can hold stakes in the exchanges and appear in their marketing. The line is drawn only at promoting contracts on NBA games.

It has been revealed that the split also shuts NFL players out of an industry that leans heavily on their sport. By the league’s own figures, football made up $1.8 billion of prediction-market trading on the season’s first Sunday. That was more than half of the day’s total.

Recent findings suggest that the league is pressing that view at the Supreme Court. On October 8, 2026, it filed an amicus brief supporting Newly introduced Jersey’s request for review in Flaherty v. KalshiEX, case No. 26-299. The NFL argued that sports prediction contracts are gambling. In its view, they are not financial swaps under exclusive federal oversight.

It has been revealed that new Jersey filed its petition on September 2, 2026. It followed an April ruling in which the Third Circuit sided 2-1 with Kalshi. The appeals court found that the CFTC has exclusive oversight of sports-event contracts.

Exclusive: Saquon Barkley tells FOS he was forced to divest his equity stake in Polymarket.

Illinois appeals Pacold injunction blocking its prediction-market licensing and tax regime

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (634 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readwrite

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A federal judge has barred Illinois from licensing, taxing or prosecuting sports event contracts listed on CFTC-regulated exchanges.
  • Recent findings suggest that illinois has lost, for now, its power to police sports event contracts traded on federally regulated exchanges.
  • The order reaches three state tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A federal judge has barred Illinois from licensing, taxing or prosecuting sports event contracts listed on CFTC-regulated exchanges. The state's appeal sends the fight to the Seventh Circuit, which already has prediction-market cases from Wisconsin.

Recent findings suggest that illinois has lost, for now, its power to police sports event contracts traded on federally regulated exchanges. Judge Martha Pacold’s order in the Northern District of Illinois turns her early-October ruling into a formal injunction. It covers contracts listed on CFTC-regulated platforms such as Kalshi and Coinbase.

The order reaches three state tools. They are the Sports Wagering Act, the criminal gambling statute and an Illinois Gaming Board internet-wagering rule. The budget’s prediction-market fees fall with the licensing rules, because they apply only to providers holding a state license. Her first ruling had left the tax question open and called for more argument on the fees.

The stakes are significant. Fiscal 2026 was the first year of the state’s per-wager tax on licensed sports wagering.

Industry observers note that the Gaming Board had already tried to act. It sent cease-and-desist letters to KalshiEX, Crypto.com and Robinhood on April 1, 2025. Polymarket received one on Jan. 27, 2026. Those letters cited the Sports Wagering Act (230 ILCS 45) and the criminal code (720 ILCS 5/28-1(a)).

Lawmakers then took a different route. Gov. JB Pritzker signed the budget containing the new framework on June 16. Under the package, which includes SB 3019, prediction markets became exchange wagers under the Sports Wagering Act and needed a Gaming Board license. Each transaction carried a tax that would climb once a licensee passed five million exchange wagers. In September, Republican Rep. Travis Weaver filed House Bill 5811 to repeal the exchange-wager tax. His bill would leave the licensing rules in place.

According to recent reports, licensed online and mobile sportsbooks face their own costs. A first license for that category costs $15 million and runs four years, with each four-year renewal priced at $1 million.

According to recent reports, courts are divided on whether state gambling laws reach CFTC-regulated sports contracts. Pacold’s order is a rare win for Kalshi and the federal regulator. Before her early-October decision, Kalshi had lost 16 federal court rulings in a row. In that opinion, Pacold found the state’s other laws in conflict with federal law because they control “what can be sold, as well as where it can be sold and to whom.”.

The CFTC sued Arizona, Connecticut and Illinois on April 2, 2026, over their actions against federally registered designated contract markets. Chairman Michael Selig said the agency would defend market participants against “overzealous state regulators.”.

There are now 5 prediction-market appeals before the Seventh Circuit involving sports-event contracts:.

· CFTC v. Wisconsin· Kalshi v. Raoul· Coinbase v. Raoul· United States v. Illinois· Ho-Chunk Nation v. Kalshi https://t.co/NH7qLf591x.

— Daniel Wallach (@WALLACHLEGAL) October 31, 2026.

For operators, the injunction offers room to keep listing sports contracts in Illinois for now. For the state, it removes a revenue stream and an enforcement path at once. Anticipating a legal challenge, legislators had kept the tax’s revenue out of their budget projections. The outcome now depends on a single appeals court.

On July 29, Judge William Griesbach ruled against the CFTC in Wisconsin, and the agency took that case to the Chicago-based court. Illinois has asked the Seventh Circuit to reverse and vacate Pacold’s order.

Nebraska voters appear to reject online sports betting despite nearly $22.5 million campaign

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (587 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readwrite

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Both linked measures to legalize mobile wagering through Nebraska's racetrack casinos trailed in unofficial returns.
  • Nebraska voters appear to have turned down online sports betting.
  • A loss would be a rare setback for the industry at the ballot box.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Both linked measures to legalize mobile wagering through Nebraska's racetrack casinos trailed in unofficial returns. A defeat would close off a new market for sportsbooks and highlights that doubts about tax relief can beat a heavily funded campaign.

Nebraska voters appear to have turned down online sports betting. Initiatives 440 and 441 would have amended the state constitution and statutes to allow mobile wagering through the state’s licensed racetrack casinos. The Secretary of State’s unofficial count, with 885 of 1,322 precincts fully reporting, had 440 trailing by about 296,000 to 354,000. The companion measure, 441, trailed by about 299,000 to 351,000. The results are not yet certified.

A loss would be a rare setback for the industry at the ballot box. Betting would stay in-person only at Nebraska’s five racetrack casinos. FanDuel, DraftKings and the racetrack operators would not gain a fresh market. Initiative sponsor Jordan McGrain called the midnight results “pretty clear.”.

Tax relief was the core of the pitch. Supporters projected more than $166 million for the state’s property tax credit fund over ten years. Opponents countered that the money would flow to out-of-state gambling companies. Nebraska presently taxes casino gaming revenue at 20 percent. Of that tax, 70 percent goes to property tax relief credits.

According to recent reports, A report commissioned by Tax Relief Nebraska, the committee behind the measures, estimated just under $87 million in upcoming state tax revenue over five years. That projection did not carry the vote. Joey Spellerberg, the state treasurer, backed the opposition and stated voters saw the promised tax benefits as negligible.

Industry observers note that should the unofficial result stand, gambling-harm arguments and doubts about tax relief would have carried a heavily outspent opposition to victory. That is a warning for future online casino and sports betting pushes in other states. It also comes as lawmakers are already restricting sweepstakes and prediction markets.

According to recent reports, the ballot route followed repeated failures in the Legislature. Lawmakers did not send a similar constitutional amendment to voters, including in 2024 and 2025. Tax Relief Nebraska then submitted more than 201,000 signatures for the amendment in late June 2026. It filed 146,000 for the companion statute. Election officials flagged possibly fraudulent signatures collected during the drive.

It has been revealed that funding also drew scrutiny. FanDuel and MGM subsidiary Roar Digital gave more than $3.5 million combined to Tax Relief Nebraska. The Legal Accountability Center asked the state’s disclosure commission to investigate. It cited the companies’ ownership in Ireland and the UK.

Industry observers note that the proposed market was tightly drawn. Each racetrack gaming operator could have offered wagering through at most two online platforms. Wagering servers would have had to be located in Nebraska. State regulators would have had until June 1, 2027, to adopt rules for online wagering.

Recent findings suggest that the count now moves toward certification. County abstracts of votes must reach the Secretary of State by November 23. State canvassers meet on November 30, 2026, at 11:30 a.m. to certify the results. Recounts in eligible races start December 2 at 9 a.m.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Email remains an important communication channel for web applications. From account verification and password resets to product announcements and customer notifications, many applications depend on email to keep owners informed.

For developers, however, implementing email functionality involves more than connecting a service and sending a message. A reliable email system needs to handle authentication, dynamic content, delivery failures, user preferences, event tracking, and integrations with other application components.

In a recent development, using an email service provider (ESP) can simplify this process. Most modern providers offer REST APIs, SMTP relays, templates, automation features, and reporting tools that developers can integrate into existing applications.

This guide explores the technical considerations involved in building email integrations, including API-based sending, webhook handling, automation workflows, and deliverability.

There are two common ways to connect an application to an email delivery service: SMTP and REST APIs.

In a recent development, SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is a standard protocol used to transfer email messages between servers. Developers can connect an application to an SMTP server using credentials and configuration settings.

REST APIs provide another approach. Instead of communicating through an email server protocol, an application sends HTTP requests to an endpoint. The provider processes the request and returns a response.

Both methods can support transactional and application-generated emails, but their implementation differs.

An application already supports SMTP configuration.

Developers want a relatively straightforward integration.

Existing frameworks or libraries provide built-in SMTP support.

An application needs programmatic control over email operations.

Developers want structured responses and error handling.

Email functionality needs to integrate with other application services.

The system requires event tracking or additional API capabilities.

The right approach depends on the application's architecture, expected email volume, and integration requirements.

An API integration allows an application to trigger emails in response to specific events.

Recent findings suggest that for example, an ecommerce application might send an order confirmation after a successful payment. A SaaS application could send an account verification message after registration.

A typical integration follows this process:.

The application detects an event.

The backend prepares the recipient and message data.

The backend authenticates with the email provider.

The provider processes the request.

The application records the response and handles any errors.

Consider a Node.js application that needs to trigger an email campaign through an API.

Some platforms, including Mailmodo, provide REST API functionality for triggering campaigns and integrating external applications with email workflows.

The following example demonstrates the general structure of an HTTP request using a campaign-triggering endpoint:.

Industry observers note that this example uses the documented Mailmodo trigger endpoint and request structure. The campaign ID and API key must be replaced with the values from the relevant account.

Notice that the API key is loaded from an environment variable rather than written directly into the source code.

This is an important security practice. Credentials should never be exposed in frontend JavaScript, public repositories, or client-side application bundles.

Not every email provider offers the same integration capabilities. Developers should evaluate providers based on their API documentation, authentication methods, supported endpoints, event notifications, and integration flexibility.

For example, Elastic Email provides a REST API that developers can use to send emails and manage different email operations from an application.

In a recent development, its API uses HTTPS requests and API-key authentication. Developers can use the available endpoints to send messages, manage campaigns, retrieve information, and configure webhook notifications.

When evaluating an email API, consider these technical requirements:.

Authentication: Check how API keys are generated, stored, restricted, and rotated.

Documentation: Look for clear endpoint descriptions, request examples, response formats, and error codes.

SDK availability: Official libraries can reduce the amount of integration code required.

Permission management: Separate credentials for sending emails and accessing account information can reduce unnecessary exposure.

API limitations: Review connection limits, request timeouts, rate limits, and account-level restrictions before deploying an integration.

According to recent reports, A provider with extensive features is not necessarily the best option for every project. The important consideration is whether its API supports the application's actual requirements.

Industry observers note that sending an email is only one part of the communication process. Applications may also need to know what happens after a message is submitted.

This is where webhooks become useful.

A webhook allows an external service to send an HTTP notification to an application when a particular event occurs.

Depending on the provider, events may include:.

For example, an application could receive a delivery-failure notification and update the corresponding email record in its database.

A basic Express.js webhook endpoint might look like this:.

According to recent reports, this is a simplified example rather than a complete provider-specific webhook implementation. A production endpoint should validate the provider's signature or other authentication mechanism and follow its documented payload structure.

Sources indicate that it should also handle duplicate events safely. Webhook providers may retry notifications when an application does not respond successfully.

An idempotent event handler prevents the same notification from creating duplicate database updates or triggering repeated actions.

Email automation connects application events with predefined communication sequences.

Instead of manually sending every message, developers can create workflows that respond to user activity.

Consider a SaaS application with the following registration process:.

The backend stores the upcoming user.

A verification email is triggered.

If the user does not complete onboarding, a follow-up message may be triggered.

A simplified workflow can be represented as:.

In a production application, email delivery should generally be handled through a background job queue rather than blocking the registration request.

A queue also makes it easier to retry temporary failures, manage sending volume, and prevent email delays from affecting the main application.

Developers should consider tools such as Redis-backed queues or framework-specific job processors when building larger systems.

Automation platforms can also help manage more complex journeys. For instance, a developer can connect application events to an external email workflow instead of implementing every communication sequence independently.

The key is to keep business logic in the application while using the email service to manage message delivery and relevant campaign operations.

A successful API response does not necessarily mean that an email has reached the recipient's inbox.

Email deliverability depends on several technical factors, including domain authentication, sender reputation, message quality, and recipient engagement.

Developers should pay attention to the following configurations.

Sender Policy Framework identifies the mail servers authorized to send messages on behalf of a domain.

A correctly configured SPF record helps receiving servers evaluate whether an email originates from an authorized source.

In a recent development, domainKeys Identified Mail adds a cryptographic signature to outgoing messages. Receiving servers can use the corresponding public key in DNS to verify the signature.

Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance builds on SPF and DKIM. It allows domain owners to publish policies for handling messages that fail authentication checks and receive reports about authentication activity.

These three mechanisms should be configured carefully, especially when an application sends emails through multiple providers.

Industry observers note that email systems generate useful operational data. However, developers should avoid treating every available metric as an accurate measure of user engagement.

For example, open tracking can be affected by privacy features and automated image loading. Click tracking may also include automated security scans.

More reliable application-level signals can include:.

These events can be connected with email campaign data to understand how communication affects application activity.

Developers should also maintain a clear separation between email delivery records and user account records. This makes it easier to investigate delivery complications without unnecessarily modifying customer data.

When collecting engagement information, applications should follow applicable privacy requirements and respect user communication preferences.

Before deploying an email integration, developers should review the following areas:.

API security: Store credentials in environment variables or a dedicated secrets manager.

Domain authentication: Configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.

Error handling: Account for failed requests, invalid recipients, and temporary provider errors.

Background processing: Use queues for asynchronous email delivery.

Webhook validation: Verify incoming notifications and handle duplicate events.

Monitoring: Track delivery failures, bounce rates, and application-level outcomes.

Testing: Test email templates across different clients and devices before production deployment.

These practices help create an email system that is easier to maintain, troubleshoot, and scale.

Email integration is an key part of modern application development, but a reliable implementation requires more than connecting an SMTP server or calling an API endpoint.

Developers need to consider authentication, asynchronous processing, webhook security, automation logic, domain configuration, and event monitoring.

Sources indicate that REST APIs are useful for applications that need programmatic control over email operations, while SMTP remains a practical option for systems that already support standard mail-server connections. Webhooks add another layer by allowing applications to respond to delivery events and revision their internal records.

By choosing an integration method that fits the application architecture and following sound security and deliverability practices, developers can build email functionality that supports both immediate communication needs and long-term application growth.

All three northeast Indiana counties reject casino, leaving HEA 1038 license with no host

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (592 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readwrite

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that voters in Allen, DeKalb and Steuben counties each rejected inland casino gambling by double digits on November 3.
  • With the measure defeated, the license created by House Enrolled Act 1038 cannot be granted by the Indiana Gaming Commission.
  • Recent findings suggest that allen County, where developers were seeking to build, carried the most weight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that voters in Allen, DeKalb and Steuben counties each rejected inland casino gambling by double digits on November 3. The single fresh license in House Enrolled Act 1038, tied to a project of at least $500 million, now has no county that can host it.

With the measure defeated, the license created by House Enrolled Act 1038 cannot be granted by the Indiana Gaming Commission. A repeat ballot is also off the table. State law bars a second public question in any county that voted the measure down.

Recent findings suggest that allen County, where developers were seeking to build, carried the most weight. The county’s election-night summary counted 102,935 votes on the question, with 40.44% in favor. In DeKalb County, 7,374 voters said no. Steuben County recorded 6,234 no votes.

Recent findings suggest that the stakes were substantial. That minimum investment had to cover both the casino and its non-gambling amenities. At least 60% of that had to be spent within two years of the award. The license also carried a $150 million fee to the state, with $50 million of it going to a fund for former host communities hurt by casino closures.

The projected public return was large as well. A study done for the Indiana Gaming Commission estimated that an Allen County casino could generate $204 million in revenue alongside its annual state tax payments. Under the act, 10% of the casino’s tax payments would have gone to the northeast Indiana regional development authority.

Sources indicate that the process hinged on the vote from the start. The commission’s July guidance said it would take applications only for a county or counties where voters approved inland casino gambling. None did.

Gaming Commission officials remarked that with no county passing the referendum, nothing happens, and that any next steps are up to the legislature. That puts operators back in front of lawmakers.

Sources indicate that lawmakers have already redrawn this map once. Instead of creating a new license, a January 22, 2026 committee version of House Bill 1038 would have relocated the Ohio County riverboat license. That inland casino could have gone to Allen, DeKalb, Steuben or Wayne County. The enacted version instead created one new license and eliminated one unused racino license. Indianapolis was kept off the list because a casino there would pull business from the existing casinos in Shelbyville and Anderson.

According to recent reports, deKalb and Steuben counties have turned away a casino in referendum votes. Allen County is still counting but 'no' is leading. https://t.co/rwMo6sIYZ2.

— Niki Kelly (@nkellyIN) November 4, 2026.

Sources indicate that the vote also lands in a state that is narrowing gambling elsewhere. House Bill 1052 lets the commission fine any operator or individual $100,000 for knowingly running an internet sweepstakes game in Indiana, starting July 1, 2026. Peer-to-peer skill-based poker is exempt. Indiana still has no legal online casinos.

Indiana was not alone on Election Day, as Nebraska voters also turned down a gambling expansion. In northeast Indiana, the act’s December 1, 2026 deadline for inland casino license applications now arrives with the commission taking no applications.

Tech Report: Arkansas sues VGW and Kalshi, citing $66 million in VGW taxable sales in one year

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (657 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readwrite

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin has sued sweepstakes casino operator VGW and prediction market Kalshi on the same day, alleging illegal gambling under state law.
  • Arkansas has opened a two-front legal fight against online gambling it states is unlicensed.
  • According to recent reports, both cases allege illegal gambling and violations of the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin has sued sweepstakes casino operator VGW and prediction market Kalshi on the same day, alleging illegal gambling under state law. The VGW complaint puts a dollar figure on the state's sweepstakes market and adds Arkansas to a growing list of states challenging the dual-currency model.

Arkansas has opened a two-front legal fight against online gambling it states is unlicensed. One lawsuit targets VGW, the company behind Chumba Casino, LuckyLand and Global Poker. The other targets KalshiEX LLC and Kalshi Inc., the companies that own the Kalshi prediction market.

According to recent reports, both cases allege illegal gambling and violations of the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act. Both also include an unjust enrichment claim. In each case the state seeks restitution, penalties, taxes and injunctive relief.

It has been revealed that the VGW suit attacks the Gold Coin/Sweeps Coin model that almost every US sweepstakes casino relies on. It names ten affiliated VGW companies. The complaint states VGW reported about $66 million in taxable Arkansas sales between July 2025 and June 2026 and paid about $6 million in sales and use tax over that period, Gaming.net reported.

Recent findings suggest that those figures show a manufacturer declaring sales to the state and paying tax on them. Yet VGW holds no Arkansas casino license, the state alleges. The complaint also accuses VGW of letting 18-year-olds play, even though Arkansas casinos require players to be 21.

The case lands less than two months after the Fresh York settlement. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced that deal on September 9, 2026. It covered Chumba Casino, Global Poker and Luckyland Slots. VGW’s coin-based games were already off the table for New Yorkers by then, after her office sent the firm a cease-and-desist letter in June 2025.

Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman went to court a few months earlier, claiming VGW’s sweepstakes casinos break Kentucky gambling law. Florida has also moved against dual-currency sweepstakes since June 2026. Arkansas now joins Kentucky, Florida and New York on that list. For operators using the same coin structure, the pattern points to rising legal exposure state by state.

Recent findings suggest that the Kalshi complaint rests on a constitutional definition. The Arkansas Constitution’s definition of casino gaming expressly covers accepting wagers on sporting events. Kalshi has never held a casino-gaming license from the state commission, the state alleges. Nor has it held any other Arkansas authorization to take sports wagers.

Sources indicate that the complaint expressly limits itself to state-law claims and relief under Arkansas law. That choice means the state is relying on its own consumer-protection statute rather than waiting on the CFTC. Money lost, betting that gets out of hand, and depression or other damage to mental health are dangers Kalshi understands its customers face, Griffin’s office mentioned.

Today I filed a lawsuit against VGW, an online gaming platform that features such games as @ChumbaCasino, LuckyLand Casino, @LuckyLandSlots, and @official_glp.

According to recent reports, arkansas’s gambling laws are clear. If you’re providing a means for Arkansans to gamble money within our state, you are… pic.twitter.com/qs2dhRMC8K.

— Attorney General Tim Griffin (@AGTimGriffin) November 4, 2026.

Filing both cases on the same day signals how Arkansas views the two products. The attorney general is treating sweepstakes casinos and sports event contracts as the same kind of unlicensed gambling. Other states may weigh whether to copy that approach.

The VGW case was filed in White County Circuit Court. The Kalshi case was filed in Independence County Circuit Court.

Recent findings suggest that A few years ago, renting a VPS meant signing up to be a part-time sysadmin. You’d SSH into a blank Ubuntu prompt and lose a Saturday to Nginx configs and firewall rules before writing a single line of your actual project.

In 2026, three things have changed. What we build has changed: AI coding tools turn weekend ideas into working apps, and AI agents need a machine that stays on after your laptop closes. Who runs servers has changed: you can now ask an AI agent in your terminal to set up a reverse proxy, close a port or work out why something broke. And what servers cost has changed: the AI boom is soaking up the world’s memory supply, and hosting prices are rising with it.

So I bought the smallest Hostinger VPS plan, deployed a Node.js app in Docker, and handed the DevOps work to Hostinger Agent, the AI assistant built into the dashboard.

Below is what that felt like step by step and whether it’s worth locking in a price before they climb further.

Sources indicate that most VPS hosting for developers now falls into four buckets. They all run on the same kind of machine; what changes is how much RAM you give them.

Industry observers note that apps built with AI coding tools. Claude Code and Cursor get you to a working Node.js or Python app fast, then leave you wondering where to put it. A VPS gives you one fixed monthly bill instead of usage-based pricing. If you want push-to-deploy, Hostinger offers Ubuntu templates with Coolify or Dokploy preinstalled.

According to recent reports, AI agents and automations that run 24/7. For most people, a “VPS for AI” means a CPU box that never sleeps, not a GPU. Think n8n workflows, a scheduled scraper, or your own agent in a Docker container. Hostinger even has an “Ubuntu 24.04 with Claude Code” template: SSH in, run claude /login, and the agent keeps working after you close your laptop.

APIs, backends and databases for side projects. A Postgres instance, a Redis cache and a small API behind a reverse proxy fit comfortably on a mid-sized proposal. You pick the versions, the extensions and the backup schedule.

Client sites and stores. Freelancers outgrow shared hosting when one client needs a custom PHP extension or a WooCommerce store starts to crawl. A VPS with cPanel or Plesk, or a WordPress or WooCommerce template, keeps client work isolated and under your control.

If you’d rather not build anything from scratch, the Docker Manager catalog listed 1,017 one-click templates when I checked, including 93 under AI/ML and 162 under Developer tools.

In a recent development, for this Hostinger VPS review, the question I cared about was simple: how long from “Choose blueprint” to an app on the internet? On KVM 1, the entry plan, it was about 12 minutes. Here’s each step with rough timings.

I went with KVM 1: 1 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 50 GB NVMe storage and 4 TB of bandwidth. On the Black Friday deal it costs $6.49/mo, paid upfront as $155.76 for 24 months, and renews at $11.99/mo.

Sources indicate that you choose the server’s location and what to install during checkout, alongside your billing details. The location picker reveals estimated latency for each data centre; mine demonstrated about 80 ms.

Recent findings suggest that install options come in three tabs: Plain OS, Control panel and Applications. I picked plain Ubuntu 26.04 LTS to see how much work the AI would take off my hands. A daily backup add-on is offered, but weekly backups are already included.

The five-minute estimate was about right. The “you’re ready” screen then gives you two ways in: the VPS dashboard, or a pre-filled ssh root@ command. It also offers a free domain for a year to use as the server’s hostname.

The overview demonstrates the OS, proposal, CPU, RAM, disk and bandwidth at a glance, with Docker Manager, Backups & Monitoring, Security and DNS Manager in the side menu.

Every server also gets a hostname under hstgr.cloud (mine was srvXXXXXXX.hstgr.cloud), which came in handy later for SSL. I’ve masked my hostname as srvXXXXXXX throughout and blurred IP addresses in the screenshots.

Plain Ubuntu doesn’t ship with Docker. Open Docker Manager in hPanel and it installs Docker for you with one click. From there you can deploy apps from a Compose file, a repository URL or the one-click catalog.

Click Web console and you’re logged in as root in a browser tab, with Hostinger Agent in a panel beside it. You don’t need an SSH client or keys. The login banner flagged 33 pending updates, 23 of them security fixes; more on that later. A quick docker --version confirmed Docker 29.9.3 was ready.

Here’s the whole app: a tiny HTTP server with a health check, and a Dockerfile on Node.js 24, a supported LTS line.

Then build it, run it and check it:.

Recent findings suggest that the build took 8.3 seconds, including pulling node:24-alpine, and the health check answered straight away. The --restart unless-stopped flag brings the container back after a crash or reboot, which I tested later.

That’s a working app, but on plain HTTP, on a high port, with no TLS. Getting it production-ready is the DevOps part I handed to the AI.

Sources indicate that an AI-managed VPS isn’t the same as a traditional managed VPS. You still get a self-managed server with full root access, but Hostinger Agent does the work you’d normally do yourself. Agent (previously called Kodee) is an MCP-powered assistant that lives in the dashboard and beside the AI web terminal, and it’s included at no extra cost. You can also connect Claude or Cursor to your server through Hostinger’s MCP server.

I gave it three tasks in plain English.

My prompt: “Check that Docker is installed, then set up a reverse proxy with a free SSL certificate so my demo-app container (port 3000) is served at https://srvXXXXXXX.hstgr.cloud.”.

It started by looking around: the Docker and Compose versions, which ports were in use, whether a web server was already running, and the OS release. Then it installed Caddy from Caddy’s official repository, configured the proxy and made sure ufw allowed web traffic.

According to recent reports, it read Caddy’s logs to confirm the Let’s Encrypt certificate, which arrived in about 6 seconds. Finally it tested its own work: HTTPS returned 200, and plain HTTP returned a 308 redirect. The whole task took about two minutes.

To give it a real fault, I ran docker stop demo-app and reloaded the site. Then I asked why it was returning a 502 and to fix it.

In a single command, it checked the container state (Exited (137)) and searched Caddy’s logs, where it found connect: connection refused on port 3000. It restarted the container, confirmed /health and HTTPS were back, and even pointed to my docker stop in the terminal history. It also explained that --restart unless-stopped covers crashes and reboots, but not a manual stop.

In a recent development, A tip it didn’t mention: exit code 137 means Docker had to force-kill the container, because Node running as PID 1 ignores SIGTERM. Add --init to docker run for clean, instant shutdowns.

It has been revealed that this was the most impressive answer. ufw already allowed only those three ports, but Agent noticed port 3000 was still reachable from the internet, because Docker-published ports bypass ufw rules.

It has been revealed that it recreated the container bound to 127.0.0.1:3000, so the app is only reachable through Caddy, and confirmed with an external port check. It left DNS, time sync and Caddy’s local admin port running, explaining that stopping them would break DNS and time sync.

Recent findings suggest that then I asked it to reboot the server. First it checked that Docker and Caddy start on boot and that the container’s restart policy was set, then it rebooted. The site came back over HTTPS without any help from me.

Nothing I asked for was destructive, so Agent just got on with it: the firewall change, the container rebuild and the reboot all ran without a confirmation prompt.

The Agent panel states so upfront, noting that terminal commands can run without one. For destructive actions such as reinstalling the OS or restoring a backup, Hostinger’s FAQ says Agent always asks for confirmation first.

One thing worth knowing: to close port 3000, Agent removed and recreated my container. That was harmless for a stateless demo, but a container that keeps data without a volume would lose it. Take a snapshot before big jobs, and keep the panel in view.

Here are the four looks at their Black Friday rates for a 24-month term.

Industry observers note that for scale, here’s what my test used. With the Node app, Docker and Caddy all running, KVM 1 had 3.3 GB of its 4 GB RAM still available, and the app container itself used about 65 MB.

Sources indicate that so 4 GB is plenty for one or two small apps. Move to 8 GB on KVM 2 once you add Coolify, a database, or n8n with its own Postgres, because those are the services that eat memory.

According to recent reports, finding a cheap VPS got harder in 2026, because memory got expensive. AI data centres are buying up DRAM, and hosts are passing the cost on. In April 2026, Hetzner raised cloud server prices by up to 37%, citing hardware costs, then raised prices again in June. On the same April date, OVHcloud’s entry VPS went from $4.90 to $7.60, a 55% jump. Nobody can promise where VPS prices go next, but the trend this year has been up.

This is how Hostinger’s Black Friday pricing works. You pay upfront for 12 or 24 months, and the 24-month term gives the lowest monthly rate. Your price is fixed for that whole term. After that, it renews at the standard rate.

Industry observers note that on KVM 2, for example, you pay $210.96 today (the $8.79/mo rate) for 24 months, and it renews at $14.99/mo after that. Do the maths on the renewal before you commit, not just the headline rate.
